text: Not every evening needs to be productive. Some evenings simply need to be lived.
One should never judge a book by its cover. Wine labels, however, are fair game.
Patience is a virtue. Particularly when the wine needs a little time and the dinner guests need considerably more.
Life is too short for bad conversation, but fortunately long enough to change the subject.
The secret to a good dinner party is excellent company, a little preparation, and knowing when to stop explaining the wine.
A screwcap is not an apology. It is a closure. Judge the glass, not the hat.
Friendship rarely requires a grand gesture. It does require that you send the message before midnight.
Your next favorite may come from a place you cannot yet find on a map. Excellent. Let curiosity do the shopping.
The perfect occasion is a suspicious invention. Clean glasses, however, are not optional.
Dry does not mean the wine will dry your mouth. Wine words enjoy a little mischief.
Some questions are best considered slowly. Others can wait until after the music starts.
Offer water with the same warmth as wine. Nobody should have to explain an empty glass.
Taste is personal. It is not a loyalty oath, and it does not require an audience.
If the saxophone begins competing with the guests, the saxophone must lose.
A valley is more than its busiest road. The slower map is often the better story.
You have quite enough passwords already. The week can begin without a new system.
